articles.summary: Ao todo, são 15 vagas em Cachoeiro e sete em Piúma. As inscrições já estão abertas e podem ser feitas exclusivamente pela internet.
articles.body:
Câmaras municipais de Cachoeiro de Itapemirim e Piúma abre concursos com salário de até R$ 9 mil no Espírito Santo — Foto: Reprodução

Duas câmaras municipais no Espírito Santo - Cachoeiro de Itapemirim e Piúma - estão com inscrições abertas para concurso público para preencher vagas em cargos de níveis médio e superior. Os salários podem chegar a R$ 9 mil.

A Câmara de Cachoeiro lançou edital para servidores efetivos. Ao todo, são oferecidas 15 vagas imediatas para profissionais com nível superior. As remunerações variam de R$ 3.412,50 a R$ 7.046,62, mais auxílio-alimentação no valor de R$ 1.314,82. A jornada de trabalho é de 30 horas semanais para todos os cargos.

As inscrições poderão ser feitas das 14h do dia 10 de novembro até as 23h59 do dia 17 de dezembro de 2026, exclusivamente pelo site do Instituto Access , banca organizadora do certame.

A taxa de participação é de R$ 100 para o cargo de procurador legislativo e de R$ 60 para as demais funções.

Os candidatos inscritos no CadÚnico ou doadores de sangue poderão solicitar a isenção da taxa nos dias 10 e 11 de novembro de 2026, na mesma página de inscrição.

O concurso público contará com provas objetivas e discursivas, de caráter eliminatório e classificatório, além de prova de títulos (apenas classificatória). Os exames estão previstos para o dia 28 de fevereiro de 2027, no município de Cachoeiro de Itapemirim e, se necessário, em cidades vizinhas.

A aplicação das provas seguirá a seguinte divisão de horários:

Manhã (das 8h às 12h): para o cargo de auditor interno público e analista legislativo nas especialidades de Direito, Financeiro e Comunicação.

Tarde (das 14h às 18h): para os demais cargos ofertados.

Os aprovados e nomeados serão submetidos ao regime estatutário (garantindo estabilidade). O concurso público terá validade de dois anos, contados a partir da data de homologação do resultado final, podendo ser prorrogado uma única vez por igual período.

Analista legislativo - especialista em Contabilidade (2)

Analista legislativo - especialista Financeiro (1)

Analista legislativo - especialista em Recursos Humanos (2 vagas)

Analista legislativo - especialista em Comunicação (1 vaga)

Analista legislativo - especialista em Direito (2 vagas)

Já a Câmara de Piúma, no Litoral Sul, lançou edital de concurso público para contratar servidores de níveis médio e superior. As remunerações variam de R$ 3.211,74 a R$ 9.018,78, conforme o cargo e a carga horária. A oferta é de sete vagas imediatas, além da formação de cadastro de reserva.

De acordo com o edital, há oportunidades para agente administrativo, agente patrimonial e almoxarife, agente de contratação, auditor de controle interno, ouvidor, procurador legislativo e tesoureiro.

As inscrições poderão ser feitas das 6 de novembro até as 18h do dia 19 do mesmo mês, exclusivamente pelo site do Instituto de Desenvolvimento Social, Gestão e Tecnologia , banca organizadora do certame.

A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 70 para os cargos de nível médio e de R$ 120 para os de nível superior.

Os candidatos inscritos no Cadastro Único para Programas Sociais do Governo Federal (CadÚnico) ou doadores de medula óssea poderão solicitar a isenção da taxa no período de 6 a 8 de novembro, no mesmo site de inscrição.

A seleção contará com prova objetiva para todos os cargos, prova discursiva para procurador legislativo e avaliação de títulos para as funções de nível superior. Os exames serão aplicados no dia 13 de dezembro de 2026.

articles.title: Chamado de 'vendido', ex-candidato à Presidência do Paraguai é expulso de protesto em meio à crise política | G1
articles.standfirst: Hostilizado na noite de quinta-feira (5), Paraguayo Cubas foi carregado e expulso das ruas por manifestantes em meio à crise bancária que levou à abertura de um processo de impeachment contra o presidente Santiago Peña.
articles.summary: Hostilizado na noite de quinta-feira (5), Paraguayo Cubas foi carregado e expulso das ruas por manifestantes.
articles.body:
O ex-candidato à Presidência do Paraguai Paraguayo Cubas , conhecido como Payo Cubas, foi hostilizado por manifestantes na noite de quinta-feira (5), em meio à crise política e bancária que atinge o país.

Vídeos que circularam no X, antigo Twitter, mostram o político sendo carregado e expulso das ruas por pessoas que participavam dos protestos. (Veja mais abaixo)

A reação também apareceu nas redes sociais.

Internautas ironizaram a recepção dada a Cubas e o acusaram de oportunismo. " Ele jurava que seria bem recebido ali", escreveu um usuário no X. Outro comemorou a expulsão do político, a quem chamou de vendido.

A hostilidade ocorre em um momento de forte insatisfação popular com a crise desencadeada pela liquidação do banco digital Ueno , que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso aos próprios depósitos.

O escândalo atingiu o governo de Santiago Peña , que foi acionista do grupo controlador da instituição até março de 2025 , e levou à abertura de um processo de impeachment contra o presidente.

Cubas, por sua vez, tem uma trajetória marcada por controvérsias .

Político de extrema direita e com discurso antissistema, ele ficou conhecido por declarações agressivas e episódios de violência durante sua passagem pelo Senado. Em 2019, perdeu o mandato após agredir um policial e fazer declarações contra brasileiros que vivem no Paraguai .

Em 2023, disputou a Presidência pelo partido Cruzada Nacional e terminou em terceiro lugar, com 23% dos votos, atrás de Peña, eleito com 43%, e de Efraín Alegre, que recebeu 27%.

Depois da derrota, contestou o resultado das eleições, alegou fraude sem apresentar provas e incentivou manifestações. Em maio daquele ano, foi preso preventivamente sob acusação de perturbação da tranquilidade pública.

A crise política no Paraguai começou após o Banco Central determinar, na terça-feira (3), a liquidação do banco digital Ueno.

A instituição tinha cerca de 3 milhões de clientes e aproximadamente US$ 850 milhões em depósitos, incluindo recursos do Instituto de Previdência Social.

O fechamento ocorreu depois que a autoridade monetária identificou insuficiência de recursos para cobrir as obrigações do banco, relacionada a empréstimos concedidos a empresas vinculadas à própria instituição.

O caso ganhou dimensão política porque o presidente Santiago Peña foi acionista do Grupo Vázquez, controlador do Ueno, até começo do ano passado.

A oposição acusa o governo de possíveis conflitos de interesse, manipulação de regras e desvio de recursos previdenciários. Também questiona a atuação do Banco Central na fiscalização da instituição.

Na quinta-feira (6), deputados aprovaram por unanimidade, com 78 votos, a abertura de um processo de impeachment contra Peña. O presidente chegou a anunciar sua renúncia, mas o Congresso não aceitou encerrar o processo dessa forma.

articles.standfirst: Evento Amazonas Solidário será realizado nesta sexta-feira (6), no Sambódromo de Manaus. Entrada será mediante a doação de dois quilos de alimentos não perecíveis.
articles.summary: O show do Filho do Piseiro no Sambódromo de Manaus arrecada alimentos para mais de 124 mil famílias atingidas pela grave estiagem e queimadas no Amazonas.
articles.body:
Filho do Piseiro antes de show no Sou Manaus 2026. — Foto: Patrick Marques/g1 AM

O cantor amazonense Filho do Piseiro é uma das atrações do evento beneficente Amazonas Solidário, realizado nesta sexta-feira (6), no Sambódromo de Manaus . A entrada será mediante a doação de dois quilos de alimentos não perecíveis, que serão destinados às famílias atingidas pela estiagem e pelas queimadas no estado.

O evento está previsto para começar às 19h. A mobilização busca arrecadar donativos para pessoas afetadas pelos impactos da crise ambiental, que tem comprometido o acesso a alimentos, água potável e serviços essenciais, principalmente em comunidades do interior.

Estiagem atinge mais de 160 mil famílias

Segundo o mais recente Boletim Operação Estiagem 2026, divulgado pelo Comitê Permanente de Enfrentamento a Eventos Climáticos e Ambientais do Governo do Amazonas, nesta sexta-feira (6), mais de 160 mil famílias estão sendo afetadas pela seca no estado. Ao todo, 47 municípios estão em estado de emergência .

Um levantamento preliminar da Defesa Civil do Amazonas, mencionado no decreto de emergência em saúde pública publicado no dia 26 de outubro, também apontou que 562 comunidades estavam isoladas em consequência da seca dos rios.

O cenário é agravado pelos impactos das queimadas. Dados do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe), apresentados no boletim estadual, apontaram 8.214 focos de calor no Amazonas entre 1º de julho e 26 de outubro.

Já o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM) informou ter combatido 24.266 focos de incêndio entre 1º de junho e 25 de outubro.

articles.title: Guarujá sanciona lei contra assédio moral e sexual no serviço público | G1
articles.standfirst: Legislação prevê denúncias anônimas, proteção contra retaliações e punições aos responsáveis. Prefeitura terá 90 dias para regulamentar as medidas.
articles.summary: Legislação prevê denúncias anônimas, proteção contra retaliações e punições aos responsáveis. Prefeitura terá 90 dias para regulamentar as medidas.
articles.body:
Prédio da Prefeitura Municipal de Guarujá, no litoral de São Paulo. — Foto: Divulgação / Prefeitura do Guarujá

Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo, sancionou uma lei para prevenir e combater casos de assédio moral e sexual no serviço público municipal . A legislação prevê ações de conscientização, proteção às vítimas e responsabilização dos envolvidos. Publicada nesta quinta-feira (5), a lei terá 90 dias para ser regulamentada pelo Poder Executivo.

A Lei Municipal nº 5.530/2026, de autoria da vereadora Dra. Adriana Machado (PSD), foi sancionada pelo prefeito Farid Madi (Podemos). Entre as medidas previstas estão campanhas permanentes de conscientização, treinamentos para servidores e gestores, criação de canais seguros e confidenciais de denúncia e proteção contra retaliações.

A administração municipal também deverá oferecer apoio psicológico e jurídico às vítimas. A lei vale para órgãos e entidades da administração pública municipal, incluindo autarquias, fundações, empresas públicas e sociedades de economia mista.

A legislação estabelece as seguintes definições:

Assédio moral Conduta abusiva, frequente e repetitiva que tenha como objetivo ou efeito degradar as condições de trabalho, ofender a dignidade ou a integridade física e psíquica do servidor ou criar um ambiente intimidatório, hostil ou humilhante.

Assédio sexual Conduta de conotação sexual não consentida que cause constrangimento, intimidação ou ofensa, incluindo palavras, gestos, insinuações, mensagens e contatos físicos indesejados.

Guarujá (SP) publica lei que previne e oferece apoio as vítimas de assédio moral e sexual nos órgãos públicos. — Foto: Marcelo Camargo/Agência Brasil

As denúncias serão anônimas e poderão ser feitas por qualquer servidor público ou terceiro que tenha conhecimento dos fatos. Os relatos poderão ser encaminhados pelo canal eletrônico da prefeitura, pela Ouvidoria Municipal ou formalmente à chefia imediata ou à comissão de ética.

A apuração ficará sob responsabilidade de uma comissão específica, formada por servidores capacitados e imparciais, com garantia do contraditório e da ampla defesa.

Entre as penalidades previstas estão advertência, suspensão, demissão e multa administrativa, quando aplicável. A punição deverá considerar a gravidade da conduta, eventual reincidência e os danos causados à vítima.

articles.title: Papa fala após de ter votado nas eleições dos Estados Unidos: 'Orgulho de ser americano' | G1
articles.standfirst: Pontífice deu declaração durante voo para Monvidéu, primeira parada de sua viagem à América Latina.
articles.summary: Pontífice deu declaração durante voo para Monvidéu, primeira parada de sua viagem à América Latina.
articles.body:
O papa Leão XIV afirmou, nesta sexta-feira (6), que se sente "orgulhoso de ser americano" após ter votado nas eleições dos Estados Unidos na última terça (3). Ele votou por correspondência no pleito de meio de mandato.

A contagem dos votos da disputa legislativa ainda está acontecendo. Porém, os resultados parciais já monstram uma avanço expressivo do partido Democrata contra o Republicano , que abriga o presidente Donald Trump .

Os democratas elegeram 20 senadores, sendo sete de virada, e chegaram a 54 das 100 cadeiras da Casa até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Na Câmara, o partido conseguiu "virar" 25 cadeiras que estavam sob o controle dos republicanos em distritos de mais de 10 estados. Somaram, ao todo, 237 das 435 cadeiras.

Leão entrou para a história como o primeiro pontífice a participar de uma eleição norte-americana.

A declaração foi feita a bordo do avião que o leva a Montevidéu, no Uruguai , a primeira parada de uma viagem de 12 dias pela América do Sul.

O papa também afirmou que está se sentindo relativamente bem após passar por uma cirurgia para tratar um câncer no pulmão no mês passado.

Aos 71 anos, o pontífice disse que a experiência com o tratamento contra o câncer reforçou sua convicção de que o acesso à saúde é um direito humano.

Leão XIV fará um dos roteiros internacionais mais exigentes das últimas décadas. Serão cerca de 31 mil quilômetros percorridos entre Uruguai, Argentina e Peru .

O papa Leão participa de uma cerimônia oficial de boas-vindas no Aeroporto Internacional de Carrasco, durante a primeira visita papal ao Uruguai desde 1988. A viagem faz parte de um roteiro de 12 dias pela América do Sul. — Foto: Yara Nardi / Reuters

O roteiro começa no Uruguai, país considerado secular. Depois, passa pela Argentina, terra natal do antecessor Francisco. Por fim, será a vez do Peru, onde Leão XIV passou anos como missionário e bispo e acabou se tornando cidadão.

O papa ficará dois dias no Uruguai, três na Argentina e quase uma semana no Peru. Durante a viagem, celebrará missas ao ar livre, que devem reunir milhões de pessoas, discursará para líderes políticos, participará de encontros com jovens e visitará comunidades remotas dos Andes de helicóptero.

A América Latina ainda é a região com o maior número de católicos do mundo. Mas a presença da Igreja Católica vem diminuindo no continente.

articles.title: Prefeito de Anhembi é cassado por suspeita de fraude em oficina | G1
articles.standfirst: Cassação foi aprovada por seis votos a três durante sessão extraordinária. Julgamento ocorreu após Justiça revogar liminar que travava apuração de gasto de quase R$ 59 mil em veículo municipal.
articles.summary: O prefeito de Anhembi, Jairo de Góis, teve o mandato cassado nesta sexta-feira (6) após investigação de irregularidades e suspeita de fraude em serviços mecânicos.
articles.body:
A Câmara Municipal de Anhembi (SP) cassou por seis votos a três, o mandato do prefeito Jairo de Góis ( Republicanos ) durante sessão extraordinária realizada nesta sexta-feira (6), com duração de oito horas. O vice-prefeito, Everton Daura Macedo, conhecido como Tom Macedo (Republicanos) tomou posse nesta mesma sessão.

O julgamento é resultado da Comissão Processante (CP) instaurada para investigar irregularidades e suspeita de fraude na contratação de manutenção mecânica de um veículo da frota pública, orçada em quase R$ 59 mil, além de omissão de respostas aos pedidos de fiscalização do Legislativo.

A votação foi autorizada após sentença proferida pelo juiz Lucas Gomes Henriques de Araújo, da 1ª Vara da Comarca de Conchas (SP), em mandado de segurança. O magistrado extinguiu os efeitos da liminar concedida à defesa do agora ex-prefeito em julho, julgou válidos os atos da comissão e fixou prazo de cinco dias para que os parlamentares definissem o caso no plenário.

A denúncia teve início em abril de 2026, protocolada por uma moradora . A acusação apontou que o município empenhou R$ 58.950,00 para uma suposta retífica completa no motor de um ônibus do Departamento de Educação.

Contudo, relatórios documentais iniciais indicavam a placa de uma ambulância com motor fundido. Além disso, a prefeitura foi acusada de descumprir prazos legais ao deixar de enviar informações solicitadas pela Câmara por meio de requerimentos oficiais.

Prefeito de Anhembi é alvo de comissão processante — Foto: TSE/ Divulgação

Durante as investigações conduzidas pelo presidente da comissão, Ivan Franco Monteiro (União), e pelo relator, Daniel Zacharias Zago ( MDB ), a apuração concentrou-se no ônibus escolar.

Um laudo pericial oficial constatou que o motor não passou pelo serviço completo faturado por dispensa de licitação: foram identificados apenas reparos pontuais em peças, enquanto pistões e blocos mantinham características originais de fábrica.

A auditoria da comissão também indicou inversão cronológica na contratação com a oficina, com abertura de demanda, empenho e parecer jurídico datados de maio de 2025, antes da realização das cotações de preços de mercado.

Questionado sobre as acusações, Jairo de Góis declarou na noite desta quinta-feira (5), antes da votação da CP, que mantinha a tranquilidade e defendeu as entregas de sua administração municipal:

"Eu estou tranquilo, que o meu compromisso é com a população. A população de Anhembi sabe o que nós adquirimos no começo do governo e sabe que a gente vem conseguindo conduzir tudo da melhor maneira possível, trazendo muitos resultados positivos até aqui. E cabe agora aos nossos nobres vereadores analisar todo o trabalho feito. Melhoramos 75% do nosso departamento de saúde, adquirimos vários veículos com recurso próprio pagamos milhões de dívida adquirida da gestão passada. E que, com 1 ano e 7 meses podemos firmar que saímos de uma situação de calamidade e já estamos caminhando pra uma Situação confortável, pra por em Prática Vários Projetos."

A reportagem entrou em contato com a defesa de Jairo, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Praça do Skate em Maceió: moradores denunciam abandono e riscos | G1
articles.standfirst: Frequentadores denunciam falta de manutenção e riscos para crianças em espaço de lazer na Ponta Verde. Prefeitura foi procurada, mas não respondeu.
articles.summary: Frequentadores da Praça do Skate em Maceió denunciam o descaso com brinquedos enferrujados, lixo acumulado e restrições no uso de banheiros e água no local.
articles.body:
Brinquedos quebrados e enferrujados, traves com risco de queda, lixo acumulado e iluminação precária estão entre os problemas denunciados por frequentadores da Praça do Skate, no bairro da Ponta Verde, em Maceió .

Segundo moradores, a falta de manutenção compromete a segurança de crianças e adultos que utilizam o espaço de lazer. (Assista acima)

O g1 procurou a prefeitura de Maceió, mas não obteve retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

A TV Asa Branca Alagoas apurou que nas quadras esportivas, os sinais de deterioração são visíveis. Uma das traves está danificada e outra foi improvisada com madeira, corda e uma estrutura com ferragens expostas. A tabela de basquete está enferrujada e sem cesta. O coreto também apresenta danos no piso e no teto.

Praça do Skate — Foto: Reprodução/TV Asa Branca Alagoas

A babá Isilane Maria, que frequenta a praça diariamente, reclama das condições dos brinquedos e teme que as crianças sofram acidentes. "Precisa de manutenção. Precisa prestar mais atenção, principalmente pelas crianças,", afirmou.

Uma frequentadora relatou que uma das traves já caiu e disse ter medo de que a estrutura atinja crianças durante as partidas de futebol.

Além dos equipamentos danificados, moradores reclamam da grama seca, do descarte irregular de lixo e da falta de iluminação adequada. Segundo uma frequentadora, o local fica mais escuro e inseguro a partir das 20h.

Outro problema apontado é a dificuldade de acesso aos banheiros. Os equipamentos químicos disponíveis são mantidos por comerciantes da praça e, segundo os frequentadores, só podem ser utilizados por quem consumir nos food trucks. Sem acesso livre aos banheiros, algumas pessoas acabam utilizando uma árvore da praça para urinar, provocando mau cheiro.

A ocupação de parte do espaço por mesas e cadeiras dos estabelecimentos também é alvo de reclamações, já que, segundo moradores, prejudica a circulação de pedestres.

Estruturas enferrujadas na praça do skate, em Maceió. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Asa Branca Alagoas

A utilização de um poço e de uma caixa d'água da praça também gera reclamações. Uma moradora acusa um comerciante de controlar o abastecimento e impedir que a água seja utilizada para irrigar os jardins.

Segundo ela, a estrutura deveria atender à manutenção da área verde, mas a vegetação permanece seca. A mulher afirma que, desde 2018, leva galões de água no próprio carro para regar as plantas.

O comerciante nega irregularidades e afirma que encontrou o poço desativado há cerca de 17 anos. Segundo ele, os comerciantes investiram aproximadamente R$ 4 mil para recuperar o equipamento e continuam arcando com os custos de manutenção.

A Prefeitura de Maceió foi procurada pela equipe de reportagem para esclarecer as reclamações sobre a manutenção da praça, mas não havia respondido até a exibição da matéria.

articles.title: Everyone blames data centers for high electricity prices. But these are the real reasons.
articles.summary: A new study finds that data centers have had only a marginal impact on residential electricity prices.
articles.body:
On Tuesday, Americans voted overwhelmingly against data centers and artificial intelligence growth. In 40 of 41 local ballot races around the country, many in the state of Ohio, voters opted to restrict or prohibit new data center constructions in their areas.

Much of the growing opposition to data centers has come from rising electricity prices , which are squeezing Americans in a time of already high prices and cost of living.

But, according to a new study by researchers at Harvard University and the University of Pennsylvania, data centers are probably having only a small effect on residential electricity prices. The researchers calculated that these operations were responsible for just 4 percent of the utility rate increases over the last five years.

News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free

"Even to me it was somewhat surprising," said Serguei Netessine, professor at the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania and one of the study's authors.

In the run-up to the elections, Democrats pointed to data centers — and Republican support for their development — as key drivers of electricity price increases. In one campaign ad , Democrat James Talarico, now senator-elect of Texas, said that Texans were "paying the price with skyrocketing utility bills." Sherrod Brown, Democratic senator-elect of Ohio, similarly argued that state residents were facing higher electricity bills due to the build-out of energy-hogging data centers.

There are certainly some areas — like in Pennsylvania, Virginia, Ohio and other states covered by grid operator PJM — where data centers have skyrocketed demand, pushing some costs onto residential customers.

But multiple studies by different researchers and organizations have failed to find a strong connection between data centers and the overall trajectory of U.S. electricity prices in recent years. Another analysis earlier this year by researchers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology found that, between 2010 and 2024, data centers increased average electricity prices for residential customers by just 2.1 percent.

Last year, research from the Brattle Group and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory found that data centers were actually decreasing costs in certain regions. And another study by the Electric Power Research Institute found that a doubling of data center capacity between 2019 and 2024 resulted in a 4 percent drop in home electricity prices.

"Depending on which techniques you use, you can identify a slight increase or decrease in prices historically" due to data centers, said Ryan Hledik, principal at the Brattle Group. "None of these are the kind of earth-shattering rate impacts you hear about."

The new Harvard and Penn study found a slightly higher impact on industrial electricity prices — the price paid by manufacturers and large facilities. For those customers, data centers were responsible for 15 percent of the price increase between 2020 and 2025. But for ordinary Americans, Netessine said, the changes simply were not substantial.

"So far we have no evidence that data centers increase prices all that much," Netessine said. Instead, he said, prices are rising due to more quotidian factors: rising gas prices, an aging electricity grid, and wildfires and hurricanes requiring improvements to the grid and recovery after disaster.

Most of the cost of generating and delivering electricity is based on large, up-front capital costs, such as the costs to build power plants, wires and transmission lines to carry that power into homes. Some areas of the United States also have excess "capacity" in the grid — meaning that the grid is overbuilt for the actual demand. In those areas, adding a data center means that large fixed grid costs are spread over more consumers. That could lower prices.

Of course, that's not the case everywhere. PJM has had booming data center growth that has also required additional build-out of the power grid. This has raised prices at power capacity auctions, and states like Maryland have seen increasing residential prices that are at least in part from this boom.

If the number of data centers continue to boom, experts say, residential prices could be affected more down the line. Data center electricity demand is expected to increase steeply over the next few years, requiring new power generation — wind, solar or natural gas — to be put onto the grid.

And residents have issues with data centers that go beyond the price of electricity. The new developments have been singled out for loud noise , polluting power generation , and for disturbing residential neighborhoods and natural landscapes. According to the Pew Research Center, more than half of Americans say that data centers are mostly bad for the environment. Others feel that the AI race — which could ultimately leave many Americans out of work — is being forced upon them.

"I think generally what we're seeing is a broader range of reasons the public has opposed data centers," Hledik said. "Concern about AI leading to loss of jobs — all of that is getting packaged together."

The facility is engineered for high-density computing, artificial intelligence and hyperscale cloud operations, with redundant power infrastructure designed to ensure reliability. articles.title: Meet Palmer Luckey, the 34-year-old billionaire who sold Oculus to Facebook for $2 billion and built a $61 billion defence technology company
articles.summary: At 24, Palmer Luckey had already experienced the kind of business success that many technology founders spend decades pursuing.
articles.body: At 24, Palmer Luckey had already experienced the kind of business success that many technology founders spend decades pursuing. He had created a virtual reality company, sold it to Facebook in a multibillion-dollar deal and then departed the social media giant two years later. His next venture took him into a different part of the technology industry. In 2017, Luckey established Anduril Industries, a defence technology company that has since attracted major private investment. Now valued at nearly $61 billion as of May 2026 as reported by Forbes. The business is expanding its manufacturing ambitions, including a planned $1 billion investment in an Ohio factory.How Palmer Luckey built his first virtual reality headset at just 16Luckey's interest in technology began long before he became known as a billionaire entrepreneur. Growing up in Long Beach, California, he spent much of his early life experimenting with electronics and modifying old video game consoles. He was home-schooled by his mother, while his father introduced him to mechanical projects and working on cars.Virtual reality gradually became his main interest. At a time when the technology was still largely associated with bulky equipment and specialist research, Luckey began collecting older headsets and taking them apart to understand how they worked. He wanted to improve their design and make the experience more accessible.His experiments eventually led to the creation of the Oculus Rift, a virtual reality headset he began developing as a teenager. Luckey was just 16 when he built an early version of the device. In 2012, he founded Oculus VR, turning his work on virtual reality hardware into a company. The project gained momentum through crowdfunding and growing interest from the technology community.Palmer Luckey’s rise after Facebook acquired Oculus in 2014Oculus attracted the attention of Facebook, which was looking to expand beyond its established social networking business. Forbes reported, in 2014, the company agreed to acquire Oculus VR in a transaction valued at approximately $2 billion in cash and stock.The acquisition placed Luckey among a new generation of technology entrepreneurs whose early projects had developed into major commercial ventures. He joined Facebook following the sale, continuing to work on virtual reality as the company incorporated Oculus into its broader technology ambitions. He did not remain away from entrepreneurship for long. Rather than returning to consumer electronics, his next company would focus on technology designed for military and national security applications.The technology behind Palmer Luckey’s defence company AndurilIn 2017, Luckey co-founded Anduril Industries. The business was established around the development of advanced defence systems, combining software, artificial intelligence, sensors and autonomous hardware.Its work covers areas such as surveillance, border monitoring, unmanned aircraft and other military technologies. The company has sought to develop systems that can collect information, identify potential threats and support military operations through integrated software and hardware.Oculus was built around creating immersive experiences for consumers, Anduril concentrated on technology intended for defence organisations and government customers. The company also adopted a different approach to developing and manufacturing its products. Over the years, Anduril has expanded its operations and attracted substantial investment from private backers.How Anduril’s $61 billion valuation boosted Palmer Luckey’s fortuneAnduril reached a valuation of $61 billion in May 2026 after raising $5 billion in a funding round. The investment more than doubled the company's valuation in less than a year, according to Forbes.Luckey's net worth also reflects his stake in the defence technology company. Forbes estimated his fortune at $5.9 billion as of November 5, 2026, placing him among the world's billionaires.Palmer Luckey's wealth and business profileAt 34, Luckey has built his fortune through two technology ventures operating in different industries. Forbes' November 2026 real-time estimate puts his wealth at $5.9 billion, although billionaire rankings can change as private company valuations and other financial assets fluctuate.His profile also reflects an unusual route into the technology business. He did not complete a university degree at California State University, Long Beach, and instead developed his first major product through independent experimentation.Forbes lists him as self-made, with a self-made score of eight. articles.title: Democratic probes to target Trump allies & donors: Family’s crypto ties to Pak, Kushner’s deals under scrutiny
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump often boasted that Silicon Valley CEOs and corporate titans were falling over themselves to
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump often boasted that Silicon Valley CEOs and corporate titans were falling over themselves to “kiss my ass” as they sought administration patronage. Now that even Republican stalwarts like Ted Cruz have acknowledged the party received an “ass-kicking” in the mid-term election, Trump admirers are hearing about the downside to being attached to the Presidential rump.Even before the votes have been fully counted, Democrat lawmakers are announcing a slew of Congressional investigations into Trump era shenanigans, amid cautionary warnings from some quarters that witchhunts should not derail legislative agenda they are now empowered to lay out. Wasting no time, California Congressman Robert Garcia, who is expected to chair the House oversight and government reform committee, has identified four principal areas for investigation: Trump's family business dealings, including cryptocurrency ventures (which has ties to Pakistan), corporate corruption and political kickbacks, alleged abuses by the Department of Homeland Security and ICE, and the handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files.“Lawyer up!” Garcia warned what he described as the "Trump crime family," announcing it would be held accountable for the "largest presidential grift in history." He also said he wants to examine the Trump family's real estate and overseas business interests, including Jared Kushner's investments, adding that family members and senior administration officials, including Stephen Miller, former Homeland Security secretary Kristi Noem and Corey Lewandowski, should expect questions.For Trump's corporate courtiers, the next two years could involve plenty of trips to Congressional hearings, none more than for Elon Musk, the Tesla/SpaceX honcho, The world’s richest man spent at least $445 million supporting Republican candidates and political committees during the midterms -- making him the biggest individual donor ever in US election – for paltry returns. Of 43 Republican House candidates he was reported to have backed, just three won. Six of the seven Republican Senate candidates he supported also lost, none worse than Ken Paxton in Texas, where Musk has enormous business interests, and where he spent $230 million only to see Democrat James Talarico romp home.On Tuesday, Musk had urged his more than 240 million X followers to "Vote red today!" but by Wednesday, that post had disappeared, along with an earlier pinned appeal supporting Republican Senate candidates. His own chatbot Grok confirmed that some posts had been deleted, amid reports that Democrats will be investigating his role in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), its access to sensitive government data, federal workforce cuts, cancelled contracts and the consequences for public services.Musk companies -- Tesla, SpaceX, xAI and others -- could also face scrutiny over federal contracts, subsidies and regulatory decisions. The reported use of Musk's Grok AI system in planning the operation to capture Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro is also likely to be scrutinized for use of private technology in military and national-security ops.Perhaps the most consequential change for corporate America will be in the Senate, where Elizabeth Warren is expected to head the Banking Committee, which, one wag remarked, is like appointing someone who has spent a lifetime studying where the leaks are to inspect the plumbing. Often taunted by Trump as Pocohontas because he felt she falsely claimed Native American heritage, her likely targets are expected to be Trump family’s cryptocurrency interests, particularly World Liberty Financial; the administration's efforts to weaken the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau which she helped establish; financial regulators and their treatment of politically connected businesses; and the relationship between major banks and the White House.Other incoming Democratic committee leaders, including Ron Wyden on Senate Finance and Richard Blumenthal on the Senate investigations subcommittee, are reported to be preparing their own inquiries. Blumenthal has already sought records from technology companies and federal regulators concerning corporate contributions to Trump's proposed White House ballroom and possible connections with favourable government treatment.Companies whose contributions or dealings likely to invite attention include Apple, Meta, Google, Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, BlackRock, Lockheed Martin, Palantir and Cisco. Nvidia and Apple reportedly committed $25 million apiece to the project, while Google/Alphabet, helmed by Sundar Pichai, is said to have ponied up $ 22 million and Microsoft, led by Satya Nadella, coughed up $ 10 million.There is very little the lame-duck President –-- who has often espoused the philosophy of “to the victor goes the spoils” -- can do to escape the scrutiny and investigations. After delivering what even Republican commentator Scott Jennings acknowledged an “ass-whupping” in the mid-terms, Democrats have arrived to spoil the party that the MAGA folks thought would never end.You use AI every day. articles.title: Investigators face major choice in JonBenét Ramsey murder probe
articles.summary: The Ramsey family hopes the 6-year-old's killer will be brought to justice.
articles.body:
In the early hours of Dec. 26, 1996, after a festive family Christmas, Patsy Ramsey walked down the stairs in her Boulder, Colorado, home to discover a terrifying ransom note telling her that her 6-year-old daughter JonBenét Ramsey had been kidnapped.

She immediately called 911 and the Boulder Police Department responded to the scene in three minutes.

The taunting two-and-a-half-page ransom note was addressed to JonBenét's father, John Ramsey, and demanded $118,000 for the safe return of his daughter.

"You stand a 99% chance of killing your daughter if you try to out smart [sic] us," the letter said. There was no sign of JonBenét or further communication from the would-be kidnappers.

A new "20/20" episode, "JonBenét Ramsey: Race Against Time, Who is 'Unknown Male 1?' -- A New Diane Sawyer Investigation" airing Friday, Nov. 6 at 9 p.m. ET on ABC and streaming the next day on Disney+ and Hulu, re-examines the case.

You can get more behind the scenes of each week's episode by listening to "20/20: The After Show" weekly series right on your 20/20 podcast feed on Mondays, hosted by "20/20" co-anchor Deborah Roberts.

Hours later, a police officer asked John Ramsey and a friend to look through the house to see if anything seemed out of place. John Ramsey discovered his daughter's lifeless body in the basement of their home.

An autopsy report determined that JonBenét had been sexually assaulted and killed by blunt force trauma to the head and strangulation, which was carried out with a makeshift corded torture device called a garrote.

With 19 new interviews, ABC News anchor Diane Sawyer and chief investigative correspondent Aaron Katersky take a fresh look at this cold case, talking with investigators, forensic scientists, genealogy experts, the Boulder Police chief and JonBenét's brothers Burke Ramsey and John Andrew Ramsey, among others.

In the weeks and months after the murder, members of the Ramsey family came under intense scrutiny by both the Boulder police and the general public. Skeptics of the family pointed to several details of the case, including the ransom note, which some close to the investigation believed was staged by a family member to cover up JonBenét's death.

The note was written on Patsy Ramsey's notepad but after numerous handwriting comparisons, only one indicated that the samples showed any similarities to Patsy's writing. The Ramsey family vehemently denied any claims they were involved in their daughter's death.

In 2008, DNA was detected on the outside of JonBenét's pajama bottoms using a new testing method called touch DNA analysis. It matched the DNA found inside JonBenét's underwear and traced to the same unknown male, and not to any member of the Ramsey family.

With this development, then-Boulder County District Attorney Mary Lacy wrote a letter to John Ramsey.

"This new scientific evidence convinces us that it is appropriate, given the circumstances of this case, to state that we do not consider your immediate family, including you, your wife, Patsy, and your son, Burke, to be under any suspicion in the commission of this crime," Lacy wrote. "I wish we could have done so before Mrs. Ramsey died."

Patsy Ramsey died from ovarian cancer in 2006 , two years before Mary Lacy's letter to the family.

Later, some Boulder officials said Lacy's letter was inappropriate for a prosecutor, and she should not have cleared the Ramseys while the investigation was ongoing.

In recent years, a new technology called single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) has made it possible to solve cold murder cases nationwide . The advanced testing can retrieve DNA from miniscule samples. Combined with genetic genealogy, it allows officials to identify suspects by matching DNA to that of distant family members in law enforcement databases, using online genetic databases.

Even with this promising new development, challenges remain for investigators. Some DNA samples obtained from the body and crime scene are very small and complex, as multiple DNA strands are mixed together, making it difficult to verifiably match with a single individual.

The current Boulder Police Chief Stephen Redfearn had never before done an interview about the Ramsey case. He sat down with ABC News' Sawyer, telling her that his department is in talks with labs that might be able to test the DNA using forensic genetic genealogy.

He said they are hesitant to send any sample until they have full confidence that the technology is advanced enough to get results that help progress the case. In some cases, if the sample is very small, it can be consumed by the testing.

"We might get lucky because we may only, in some circumstances, with what we have, have one shot at getting it tested," Redfearn said.

Redfearn said they are re-interviewing suspects, testing new evidence and pursuing every lead.

"I would love nothing more than 30 years since this little girl was murdered in her own home, someone finally decides to get something off their chest," he said.

Burke Ramsey, who has largely stayed out of the public eye since his sister's death, praised his parents for how strong they were in the aftermath of the tragedy.

"This awful thing happened to this family, and the world turns against you. And it's cruel," he said.

JonBenét's older half-brother, John Andrew Ramsey, said investigators must have courage and act aggressively to get the case solved as soon as possible.

"I know we're going to find this person," he said. "This is a case that can be solved. There's a mountain of evidence out there. We've got the DNA testing that's in our favor. It's not a question of if, but when."

articles.title: An Adelaide man built a cheese-making facility in his backyard without approval; after ignoring a court order to remove it for 5 years, he was found in contempt and ordered to pay over A$120,000
articles.summary: An Adelaide retiree has been ordered to pay more than A$120,000 in court costs after spending five years failing to remove an unauthorised cheese-making
articles.body: An Adelaide retiree has been ordered to pay more than A$120,000 in court costs after spending five years failing to remove an unauthorised cheese-making facility built in his suburban backyard. John Kitsis was found guilty of contempt of court after repeatedly ignoring orders requiring him to dismantle the operation at his West Croydon home. The dispute began when local authorities discovered the structures and dairy-making equipment without the necessary planning approval. Although the court gave him a deadline to comply, the facility remained in place for several years.Why was the Adelaide backyard cheese-making facility ordered to be removedAs reported by ABC News, the dispute dates back to April 2018, when the City of Charles Sturt council received a complaint about unauthorised structures and dairy manufacturing equipment at Kitsis's property in West Croydon, Adelaide.The complaint reportedly came from a person claiming to be a neighbour. It prompted council officers to investigate the property and establish whether the structures and proposed business had received the necessary approvals.During the investigation, Kitsis told council officers that he had permission to operate a cheese-making business but had not yet started the operation. Earlier court judgments also recorded that he had submitted a food business notification to the council, which acknowledged receiving the paperwork.However, submitting a food business notification did not mean that the construction itself had been approved. The council's investigation found that the cheese-making facility had been built without the required planning permission.A further inspection in September 2018 revealed that a garage and rumpus room at the rear of the property had been converted into what council staff described as a self-contained residence. The converted space included built-in cooking appliances and laundry facilities.These findings eventually led to legal proceedings over the unauthorised development.What did the court order Kitsis to do in 2020In March 2020, the Environment, Resources and Development Court ordered Kitsis to remove the unauthorised cheese-making equipment from his property. The order covered the appliances and other facilities used for dairy production, including built-in cooking, storage and preserving equipment.The court gave him 30 days to comply with the directions. However, the order was not followed within the required period, and the matter continued for years.The court later examined the prolonged failure to carry out the removal. Senior Judge Michael Durrant found that Kitsis had deliberately disobeyed the directions.The delay became a central issue in the contempt proceedings. The original removal order had been issued in 2020, but the required work was not completed until June 2025.By then, Kitsis had already been found guilty of contempt of court in February 2025. His eventual compliance therefore came several months after the contempt finding. Judge Durrant considered the length of the delay particularly serious, noting that the original order had allowed only 30 days for compliance.How did Kitsis explain his failure to follow the ordersDuring the proceedings, Kitsis offered an explanation for why he had not complied with the court's directions. According to ABC News, he arrived in Australia from Greece in 1990 and did not speak English. He suggested that this had made it difficult for him to understand what was happening during the legal proceedings.However, Judge Durrant did not accept that explanation as sufficient reason for the prolonged non-compliance.The judge was satisfied that Kitsis knew about the court orders and understood what he was expected to do. He also pointed out that Kitsis had family members who could communicate in English.Court records showed that Kitsis had communicated with both the City of Charles Sturt and the court, sometimes through his son and sometimes directly. This correspondence was considered evidence that he had been aware of the proceedings and the requirements placed on him.The case also involved earlier difficulties in getting Kitsis to attend court. He had been arrested after failing to appear and had spent 3 days in custody at the Port Adelaide police cells on one occasion.Judge Durrant described that step as regrettable but necessary, given the repeated failure to respond to the court process. The judge also gave little weight to Kitsis's apology. It was made at the last minute and did not demonstrate a voluntary expression of regret or genuine remorse for ignoring the orders.Why did the court impose more than A$120,000 in costsIn his ruling, published in December 2025, Judge Durrant described the contempt as being at the higher end of seriousness. He said Kitsis's failure to comply had been wilful and criticised the fact that the removal order had remained unfulfilled for more than 5 years.The court also considered whether Kitsis had gained any financial advantage from continuing to operate the facility. During the proceedings, he told the judge that although he had operated a cheese-making business from the premises, it had never successfully got off the ground.According to his account, the business had generated no sales and had been unsuccessful. The court therefore considered his explanation when assessing the circumstances surrounding the contempt.Despite the seriousness of the conduct, Judge Durrant took Kitsis's personal financial circumstances into account. The retiree was elderly, had limited income and was receiving a pension. For these reasons, the judge decided against imposing an additional penalty beyond the time Kitsis had already spent in custody.However, that did not remove his responsibility for the legal costs arising from the proceedings. The judge noted that Kitsis had already been ordered to pay substantial costs to the City of Charles Sturt council.He also directed him to pay further costs to the Registrar of the Environment, Resources and Development Court. The amount was set at A$123,266.36, taking the total financial consequences of the prolonged dispute beyond A$120,000.The case eventually reached a conclusion after Kitsis removed the unauthorised cheese-making equipment in June 2025. However, completing the removal did not erase the earlier failure to follow the court's directions.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump appoints Stephen Miller as chief of staff after GOP’s midterm defeat, sacks Susie Wiles
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump has named his longtime aide and current deputy White House chief of staff Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, replacing
articles.body: US president Donald Trump has named his longtime aide and current deputy White House chief of staff Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles, days after Republicans suffered a setback in the midterm elections.Trump announced the decision on his social media platform, Truth Social, on Friday, saying Miller would assume the position on Monday, November 9, 2026.“I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026,” Trump wrote.He also praised Wiles, who became the first woman to serve as White House chief of staff, saying she had “done an outstanding job” and would move to his political organisation.“I want to thank her for her service as Chief of Staff — She has done a great job!” Trump added.Wiles subsequently confirmed her departure in a post on X, saying Friday would be her last day in the role. She also indicated that her association with Trump would continue.“Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honor of a lifetime. I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First,” she wrote.“While my role may be changing, my commitment to the President and the mission never will,” she added.The leadership change comes days after Republicans suffered a major setback in Tuesday’s midterm elections, losing control of Congress. Wiles’ departure also follows reports that she could leave the position after the elections. Trump had dismissed speculation about her replacement in mid-October, saying there was “zero chance” he was considering such a move.Miller, one of Trump’s closest and longest-serving advisers, has been a central figure in shaping the administration’s hard-line immigration policies, including its deportation agenda. He currently serves as Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy and as a homeland security adviser.He joined Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign as a speechwriter and subsequently served as an adviser and Director of Speechwriting during the Republican leader’s first term. Before that, Miller worked on Capitol Hill as an aide to Republican lawmakers, including former Senator Jeff Sessions of Alabama, who later became Trump’s first Attorney General.Wiles, a veteran political strategist and longtime Trump adviser, was the longest-serving White House chief of staff during his presidency. Trump had gone through four chiefs of staff during his first four-year term.Her departure also comes months after she publicly disclosed her breast cancer diagnosis in March 2026. Following months of treatment, she indicated in October that there was no longer evidence of the disease.Miller’s appointment places one of Trump’s most trusted policy advisers in a central coordinating role within the White House, particularly as the administration prepares to navigate the political consequences of the midterm results. He is scheduled to take charge on November 9, with Wiles expected to continue working with Trump through his political operation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Waterford: Child, 6, dies weeks after arson attack on family home
articles.summary: The attack happened last month at the family home on the outskirts of Waterford in the Republic of Ireland.
articles.body:
A six-year-old boy who was critically injured in a suspected arson attack at his family home in County Waterford has died.

Elliot English died on Friday at Children's Health Ireland (CHI) hospital in Crumlin in Dublin.

His parents, Kim English and Philip English, and two of his siblings, 12-year-old Callum and nine-year-old Jayden, died in the house fire on Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford on 13 October.

Another child, who was also critically injured in the attack, remains in hospital.

A multiple murder investigation was launched by Gardaí (Irish police) following the fire.

In a brief statement on Friday, Irish police said: "The thoughts of all members of An Garda Síochána are with the extended English family at this sad time."

A number of people arrested by police in connection with the attack have all been released without charge.

In the days after the attack, hundreds of people attended a prayer vigil .

articles.title: ICE arrests Wisconsin state patrol trooper with pending asylum case at airport, attorneys say
articles.summary: The 21-year-old came to the country legally as a child from South Africa and is included in his father’s asylum application, according to attorneys.
articles.body: ICE detained a Wisconsin state patrol trooper with a pending asylum case at an airport, his attorneys said Thursday. Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe, an asylum-seeker from South Africa who has a valid federal work authorization, was detained by ICE as he waited to board a domestic flight, according to a statement from the Christopher & De Leon Law Office released Thursday and obtained by NBC affiliate WEAU. He is currently being held at a detention facility in Juneau, Wisconsin, ICE records show. According to the attorneys’ statement, Van Der Merwe tried to explain that he had a valid work permit and has a asylum application, but the ICE officers “said they did not care, placed him in handcuffs and shackles, and transported him to immigration detention.” The 21-year-old came to the country legally as a child from South Africa and is included in his father’s asylum application, according to the statement. He has been a Wisconsin state patrol trooper for nearly a year, his attorneys said. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said in a statement to NBC News, “To be clear: work authorization or a pending application do not confer legal status in the U.S.” ICE arrested Van Der Merwe during a targeted enforcement operation at the Dane County Regional Airport in Madison, Wisconsin, on Thursday, DHS said in a statement. “He entered the country in March 2019 with legal permission to stay until September 2019,” the spokesperson said in the statement. “In defiance of our nation’s laws, he overstayed his admission. This illegal alien will receive due process and remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings.” “This administration is working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport,” the spokesperson said. Attorney Marc Christopher, who represents Van Der Merwe, said in a statement that the arrest was “inhumane and despicable.” “Putting a Wisconsin State Trooper behind bars while his asylum case sits unresolved does not make our communities safer,” he said. In another statement, Christopher said, “Wisconsin trusts Carel to protect the public.” “DHS owes his family and our community an explanation of why keeping him behind bars is necessary,” he said.

articles.summary: Newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria received emailed bomb threats Friday from a purported \"Mikhail Andropov\", claiming responsibility for a widening wave of
articles.body: Newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria received emailed bomb threats Friday from a purported "Mikhail Andropov", claiming responsibility for a widening wave of hoax threats disrupting passenger flights across Europe.The messages, sent to Bulgaria's Nova TV and the Irish public broadcaster RTE, which evacuated its offices and suspended programming, were headlined "Message to the West" and portrayed the threats as the prelude to a series of attacks on means of transport across Europe. The British broadcaster Sky also said it had received a security threat. Reuters was not able to establish the identity of the sender, the origin of the emails, or whether they had in fact come from the same source as the threats to any or all of the dozens of flights affected since Tuesday.But they added to concern among European officials that the hoaxes are part of a campaign of "hybrid" disruptions, which many have blamed on Russia, aimed at countries that have helped Ukraine. Moscow has denied involvement. Spanish foreign minister Jose Manuel Albares said Europe appeared to be facing "hybrid aggression and a form of psychological warfare". Around half a dozen flights were disrupted in some way Tuesday and more than two dozen Thursday.On Friday, an Italian airport authority source said a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome had been diverted to Venice but, despite more than a dozen hoax threats, overall there was far less direct disruption to air travel. Hungarian jets did, however, escort airliners flying from Brussels to Sofia and from Prague to Bucharest and Cyprus through Hungarian airspace.Defence minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said Nato had ordered some air patrols in the area, the first report that the Western defence alliance had become involved.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bernie Sanders thinks Medicare-for-all bill could pass, 'not absolutely certain' Trump would veto
articles.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., said he's not certain President Donald Trump would veto Medicare-for-all legislation, arguing the president is "a good politician."
articles.body: Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., said in an interview Thursday he wasn't "absolutely certain" President Donald Trump would reject Medicare-for-all legislation, despite skepticism from MS NOW host Chris Hayes about the proposal's chances of becoming law. "Healthcare is a human right. We need Medicare-for-all, which is now supported by over 60% of Americans, probably 80-90% of Democrats," he said. Hayes interrupted. BERNIE SANDERS ADMITS DEMOCRATS FAILED WORKING-CLASS VOTERS ON ECONOMICS, DRIVING THEM TO DONALD TRUMP "But let me just stop you there, senator, because, I mean, obviously, I know you believe in this. I've looked at the polling. It's very clear polling on Medicare-for-all has gone up," Hayes said. "It was very interesting that Abdul El-Sayed was attacked for a million things in that race, but not for that. "But, I think you and I would agree, the odds of Donald Trump signing that into law, pretty small. ... You're going to have Senate and House, right?" Sanders disagreed and pushed back at Hayes. "Hold it, hold it, hold it, hold it, hold it, hold it. Two points. Point No. 1: Trump has the constitutional right to veto if he wants to do it. But we have the constitutional right to represent the American people and to pass the damn thing and to show the American people that we are sick and tired of maintaining a broken system. "No. 2. You know what? Donald Trump may be a bit crazy, but he is not stupid," Sanders continued. "And he is a good politician. And if this guy looks out all over the country, and he says, 'Oh my God, everybody knows the system is broken. You know what, what do I got to lose?' So, I am not absolutely certain that Trump would not sign it. "But whether he would or not, our job is to produce it. He wants to veto it, Republicans want to sustain that veto, that is their responsibility. The American people will see it." Sanders has been pushing for Medicare-for-all for years, and support for it has become more mainstream in the Democratic Party. TRUMP PLEDGES TO VETO 'INSANE' DEM BILLS, PINPOINTS ISSUE PARTIALLY TO BLAME FOR REPUBLICAN LOSSES Psychotherapist and author Jonathan Alpert told Fox News Digital in a statement that Sanders had been "giving the same speech for decades." "He knows how to tap into people's frustrations, but calling health care a human right doesn't automatically make Medicare-for-all the answer," Alpert said. "Now, Bernie is saying Trump 'may be a bit crazy, but he is not stupid' and calling him 'a good politician.' That's quite a compliment coming from someone who's spent years attacking Trump. Even Bernie seems to recognize what many Democrats refuse to admit: Trump is a skilled politician who knows how to read the public. "And Bernie knows exactly what he's doing," Alpert continued. "He's appealing to Trump's ego, dangling the possibility of a historic political victory. It's a clever bit of psychological maneuvering. Bernie may think Trump is crazy, but apparently he's smart enough to know that flattering him might get him further than attacking him. Other politicians may want to take a cue from Bernie." TRUMP CONGRATULATES DEMOCRATS AFTER DOMINANT MIDTERMS, SAYS HE LOOKS FORWARD TO WORKING WITH THEM CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Sanders made the comments after Democrats' wave of huge victories in Tuesday's midterms, winning back control of the House and the Senate. Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment.

articles.title: Jehovah's Witness rules on blood transfusions have changed, but it's too late for my brother
articles.summary: Jehovah's Witness leaders relaxed strict rules on blood transfusions, but the change came 23 days too late for Isaac Valdez.
articles.body:
In August this year, 26-year-old Isaac Valdez had an epileptic seizure while browsing in his local library, causing him to convulse and strike his head against the ground.

He lost consciousness. Later, in hospital, it transpired Isaac had hit his head with such force it had led to a brain haemorrhage.

Treatment was seriously complicated by the fact that, as a Jehovah's Witness, Isaac carried a "No Blood" card, an indication that he would not accept treatment involving any form of blood transfusion because of his religious beliefs.

As a result, a procedure to drain fluid from Isaac's brain did not take place.

But his family, from Waxahachie, Texas, were encouraged by the fact that he regained consciousness and even started to talk again. He was able to confirm that he stood by his "no blood" beliefs.

The family's relief at his apparent improvement was short-lived. Isaac slipped into a coma and his condition worsened rapidly.

A neurosurgeon told Isaac's family the only way to save his life was an emergency operation, but that it was one that required blood transfusion.

His family took the decision to abide by Issac's wishes as a lifelong Witness not to accept such a procedure.

Isaac - who his twin brother Jacob Valdez describes as an intelligent man who loved volunteering and helping the elderly - died on 26 August 2026 when doctors turned off his life support.

Just 23 days later, the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body announced a seismic change in teaching that would, in effect, have given Isaac the religious green light to have the life-saving treatment he had refused.

The change suddenly means the vast majority of medical procedures using donated blood are no longer prohibited to followers. Now, decisions on whether to accept such treatments are to be left to individuals.

Jacob, already dealing with the death of his twin, was angered at the Jehovah's Witnesses' leadership for not coming to their conclusion sooner. He told BBC News he believes Isaac could well still be alive if they had.

The original rule on blood transfusions dates back to 1945, towards the very end of a war during which the use of blood transfusions had been increasingly widespread. The leaders of Jehovah's Witnesses announced that their believers were not permitted to accept transfusions.

This was based on their interpretation of Bible verses from both the Old and New Testaments prohibiting the consumption of blood, including one from the Book of Acts that instructs believers to abstain from blood, from food offered to idols, and from things that had been strangled.

So, why has the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body, based in New York state, now decided to change the rules, 81 years after introducing them?

It comes after years of pressure from both within and outside the faith, but that is not how leaders of the faith describe the decision.

"The change is basically the application of Bible principles to modern medicine and its methods," says the Jehovah's Witnesses international spokesperson, Paul Gillies, who described it as both a fresh look at scripture and at medical advances.

We meet Gillies at the Jehovah's Witnesses UK headquarters set in 85 acres of Essex countryside. It is a vast modern complex where hundreds of volunteer followers of the faith live and work without pay.

He insists the basic teaching has not changed and that the transfusion of whole blood is still prohibited. However, for decades, most transfusions have not used whole blood, instead using the specific components of blood that are needed by the patient.

The change is being justified by permitting the use of blood components, like plasma and red blood cells and platelets, in the huge numbers of medical procedures that were previously banned.

Gillies says the Bible references "abstaining from blood" but not "various components that could be extracted from blood".

He says the Governing Body felt it their duty to avoid scriptural "overreach" and only apply what was specifically described in the Bible.

But that explanation has stunned many and led them to ask if it was not a huge overreach 81 years ago to ban blood transfusions in the first place, when transfusions are not specifically mentioned in the bible.

Others are then also asking why it has taken so long to come to this landmark decision, given that transfusions that do not use whole blood have been the norm for decades.

These are questions Jacob asked as soon as the ban was lifted, just days after a memorial service for Isaac.

Jacob, who had already left the Jehovah's Witness faith he was brought up in, texted prominent figures from Isaac's congregation in Texas after Isaac's death. The messages are full of angst, and painful to read.

He asked them to consider "the part you played in encouraging so many people to sacrifice their life for something that was never God's will".

Most did not reply, but one "elder" responded saying he could not understand why Jacob was so angry and fixated on the policy shift.

This all further infuriated Jacob, who particularly wants the faith's decision-makers to be accountable for all the lives lost.

"I want to ask them if they could apologise directly, I would like not to have a deflected answer, just straightforward apology," he says.

It is extremely difficult to say how many Jehovah's Witnesses, among the estimated nine million followers of the faith worldwide, died each year having refused treatment involving blood transfusions. But research in one medical journal in 2016, The Obstetrical & Gynecological Survey, put the figure at around 1,100.

"We're sympathetic to their feelings, and if individuals have lost family members and are concerned about some of these questions, they deserve to be heard compassionately," says Gillies.

But there was little clarity about why the change did not come earlier.

"Why has it taken this time? Well, I guess because it takes time, it doesn't necessarily mean that there is some magic change that's taken place," says Gillies.

And when asked, Gillies deflects calls for the leadership to apologise, saying that many lives had, in fact, been saved because faithful Jehovah's Witnesses had not been exposed to blood contamination scandals.

He also insists that even after the new edict, some Jehovah's Witnesses could still decide they did not want to accept a transfusion, and that may have been the case even if the edict had come years ago.

Indeed, the BBC spoke with Alex Ball, 58, a Jehovah's Witness from West Sussex, who says in 2012 a doctor told him he would not survive the chemotherapy he needed to treat his blood cancer unless he also had a transfusion.

"I wanted to adhere as closely to the scriptures as possible when I was sick, and I think I did that well."

With help from what is called "a Jehovah's Witness Hospital Liaison Committee", Alex found an American consultant who could perform a treatment to boost Alex's blood cells without the need for any products from someone else. His UK consultant agreed to treat him using the new method and it worked.

More than a decade later, Alex says he would make the same decision again, despite the change in blood policy that would have permitted the transfusions he had been told he needed.

It is not just receiving blood which has been an issue.

Elisha Cummings, 50, a Jehovah's Witness from Trinidad and Tobago, was unable to donate blood to her aunt, who died, because of the rules.

They also cost her her marriage too, with her husband of 10 years leaving the faith and divorcing her after it came to light that he had had a blood transfusion as a child, something that was looked down upon in her Witness community.

"Since the blood policy change, I have not been myself," she says. "It left me in a sort of depressed mode."

"How many houses did I go to trying to convince people about the blood doctrine? And you're coming now and it's something totally different," Elisha says.

Elisha says her beliefs as a whole have been shaken, yet she feels reluctant to leave the faith, partly because it is what provides her with her community and she fears isolation.

In the past, those who disagreed with "blood doctrine" were ostracised or felt like they needed to leave the faith. Will they now be able to come back?

"Any individual that wants to come back to the faith is warmly welcomed," says Gillies, speaking of those who had left the faith because they had accepted a transfusion for themselves or a relative.

"If they would like to become one of Jehovah's Witnesses again and would like to speak to the elders, then they're very welcome to do so."

The pressure on the Church of England to ditch its slavery reparations plan

We thought Gen Z had started going to church in droves. But the truth is more complicated

articles.title: EU prosecutor office investigates fatal train crash in Spain
articles.summary: The EU office carries out probes at Spanish rail network administrator, safety agency and state auditors.
articles.body:
The European Union’s public prosecutors have launched a probe into possible fraud in the financing of Spain’s rail network after a high-speed train crash killed at least 69 passengers last month.

The European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) said on Friday that it had carried out investigations ‌at the headquarters of Spain’s railway infrastructure manager, its railway safety agency and its court of auditors to determine possible fraud in the financing of the ⁠Madrid-Seville high-speed line.

“Today, the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) in Madrid (Spain) is conducting investigative measures at the Administrator of Railway Infrastructure (ADIF), the State Railway Safety Agency (AESF) and the Court of Auditors in Spain,” a statement from the prosecutors said.

“This comes after the opening of an investigation into possible fraud affecting EU funds allocated to the renovation and upgrading of safety, signaling and communications systems on the Madrid-Seville high-speed railway line,” the EPPO added.

Spain’s rail infrastructure manager, Adif, confirmed the visit from the EPPO to the Reuters news agency, stating that it complied with the search and provided any requested information. The other two organisations did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment.

The October 28 train collision in Urda, Toledo province, was the second fatal crash this year and led to the resignation of Transport Minister Oscar Puente .

The EPPO had already carried out a probe into the Spanish rail network in March, after a high-speed train crash in the Adamuz region killed 46 passengers in January.

There are no updates on this investigation, which looks into how the EU funds for track maintenance were used on the network line.

EU Transport Commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas expressed concern at a news briefing on Wednesday over the proximity of the two fatal accidents, calling it “very worrying” and “not something we want to see”.

Tzitzikostas also noted that Spain reached out to the European Union Agency for Railways (ERA) to assist with an ongoing national investigation.

Puente resigned on Tuesday, in what he described as a “matter of political dignity”, and Adif President Luis Pedro Marco de la Pena quit the next day. Spain’s Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo will fill in for Puente’s role until the elections in Spain later this month, which could be hampered and influenced by last month’s tragedy.

At the end of October, soon after the crash in Urda, survivors from three of Spain’s most fatal train crashes gathered to demand better safety procedures and larger investment into network maintenance to avoid further tragedies.

“Now we have seen three dreadful crashes in Spain, at Angrois, Adamuz and Urda. They will keep happening if we do not act,” train crash survivor Cristobal Gonzalez told Al Jazeera .

“At Angrois, the driver was going too fast; at Adamuz, an investigation said there was a problem on the track; and at Urda, it might have been human error and a problem with the control system. Whatever, we must stop these crashes happening by investing more in safety,” he added.

The Angrois accident in 2013, which killed 79 people, is Spain’s deadliest rail crash in modern times.

articles.title: The new Diwali luxe: Statement walls, metallic textures and the art of gold leafing
articles.summary: Beyond being merely a festive time, Diwali has historically been known for the celebration of light, joy, and rebirth.
articles.body: Beyond being merely a festive time, Diwali has historically been known for the celebration of light, joy, and rebirth. At present, luxury interior design is leaning towards a more refined and elegant festive look, where statement walls, metallic texture accents, and handmade finishes altogether give a feeling of refined, unique, and long-lasting spaces.Luxury is not merely about putting on some shine; it is also about producing layers, personalities, and an emotional connection between the artistry of the maker and the aesthetic of the design.Statement walls: The new centrepieceAesthetically speaking, statement walls are the new thing in interior decorations which bring in a lot of change in the interiors via texture, leafing metallic finishes (such as gold leafing), and other kinds of decorative features. Placed at the back of the couch, between the dining room tables or even on one of the bedroom walls, a well-placed and creatively done feature wall is capable of dictating the general mood that a particular place is to have. Gold leafing introduces a fascinating light and shadow play, a feature that allows surfaces to switch from an antique-like softness to a bright and rich look.Leafing with metallic textures and creating a feel of timelessnessA choice of leafing in gold, champagne, silver, copper, and antique kinds is among the finishes that can be used to add depth and elegance to any modern interior. Gold leafing has the virtue of creating warmth and grandeur, whereas that of champagne is more of an unassuming kind of sophistication. The use of silver leafing is great if one wants to bring out a modern palette. The leafing in copper, on the other hand, adds rich and earthy colours. If it is possible that the material is stone, wood, fabric, or the lighting design is not too flashy, then these finishes will definitely do a great job of improving the interiors without being a visual disturbance.The art of leafing with goldGold leafing represents the meeting of traditional craftsmanship and modern design. Unlike uniform metallic paint, hand-applied leafing can create subtle variations, layered textures, and distinctive artistic character. articles.title: CDC reports more than 5,000 measles cases, highest number in 35 years
articles.summary: Children and teenagers make up almost 60 percent of confirmed cases.
articles.body:
A total of 5,182 confirmed measles cases have been reported in the United States to date in 2026, according to data released by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The figure for the highly contagious but vaccine-preventable disease is the highest number reported by the CDC since 1991.

Children below the age of five make up 18 percent of cases, while children between ages five and 19 account for 41 percent of cases.

In total, children and teenagers account for about 59 percent of confirmed cases.

The majority of cases, a total of 4,993, were outbreak-associated.

The outbreak comes as vaccination coverage among US kindergarteners has decreased from 95.2 percent during the 2019-2020 school year to 92.4 percent in the 2025-2026 school year.

The number of confirmed cases by November 2026 is more than double the 2,289 confirmed measles cases reported in 2025.

According to CDC data, four people have died due to measles in 2026.

However, the agency’s national death toll is lower than the number of measles-related deaths reported by state officials, particularly in Pennsylvania, the state hardest hit by the outbreak.

Pennsylvania’s Department of Health reported six deaths and 1,487 cases this year.

The federal count has been at the centre of a dispute between Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro and US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr over how measles deaths are classified.

Pennsylvania reports “measles-associated” deaths after a person with confirmed measles dies within 30 days of developing symptoms, unless the death resulted from an unrelated event.

In August, Pennsylvania reported that two unvaccinated people died of measles. The CDC initially included the deaths in its national tally but subsequently removed them after Kennedy, a vaccine sceptic, questioned whether measles had caused or contributed to the fatalities.

The CDC has said it is working with the US Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to establish a standardised definition for measles deaths.

Infectious disease experts warn that the dispute over how to classify the deaths puts the CDC at odds with a longstanding approach to tracking the consequences of measles.

Epidemiologists have told Al Jazeera that tracking “measles-associated” deaths has long been a standard used by the World Health Organization and the CDC.

The US declared the virus eliminated more than two decades ago. Measles cases have also increased globally , particularly in communities that are vaccine-sceptical or where there are gaps in healthcare access.

Experts warn that declining vaccination rates in one geographic location can leave people thousands of miles away vulnerable, making measles prevention a shared global responsibility.
